parsed.attack: This product dies every June and the dying is total. The unit is a class group bound to one set text on one exam timetable: results day dissolves the social graph, the cohort leaves school permanently, and the moat has to be rebuilt from zero with a new intake each September. Inside the term it is worse than annual churn suggests - annotation behaviour is 90/9/1, so one keen student writes all the notes, the other twenty read, and once they notice every note on Act 3 has the same name on it, the page stops being worth opening. Their own floor, three student-written annotations per class per term, is an admission that the shared artifact may never reach the density that makes anyone return, and a monthly subscription billed to sixteen-year-olds who need it for eight weeks has one renewal in it at most.
parsed.strongest_defence: Term-time use is genuinely dense while it lasts - a set text is read over weeks, with mocks and a final exam as scheduled spikes, and the notes that matter most surface precisely at revision time. Schools are a replenishing channel rather than a churn problem: the teacher, not the student, is the retained account, and the same class link is reissued to a new cohort every September against the same text, so the annotation corpus compounds across years even though the students do not.
parsed.verdict_reason: The whole social graph and the paying cohort expire on a fixed annual date, and within the term the 90/9/1 problem means most users never build anything they would miss.
